github.title: GitHub
github.help: Connect a GitHub webhook. PRs and commits that mention an issue (<id>{example}</id>) in the branch, title or description get linked to it.
github.steps: In GitHub: repo Settings, Webhooks, Add webhook. Content type application/json, events Pull requests and Pushes.
github.secretOnce: Copy the secret now. It will not be shown again.
github.secretHidden: Saved and encrypted. Generate a new one if you lost it.
github.onOpenMove: Move the issue to In progress
github.adminOnly: Only an admin can change the integration.
github.invalidRepo: Check the repos: the format is owner/repo.
github.noLinks: No PR or commit mentions this issue.
github.regenerateConfirm: Generate a new secret? The current one stops working right away: GitHub deliveries will fail until you paste the new secret in the webhook.
github.disconnectConfirm: Disconnect GitHub? PRs and commits will no longer be linked to issues.
github.moveHelp: Only issues in the branch, in the title or after fixes, closes or resolves in the description change status.
github.connectNote: Next you'll get the URL and secret to paste into GitHub.
github.dangerHelp: A new secret invalidates the current one. Disconnecting stops linking PRs and commits.
github.statusRulesHint: What happens when a PR opens or merges
github.refOnly: Linked with ref: merging does not move the issue
github.appHelp: Install the app on your GitHub organization or account and pick the repos. Events from those repos arrive without setting up a webhook by hand.
github.rulesHelp: Pick the status each team moves to when a pull request is drafted, opened, sent to review or merged. Without custom rules, a team uses the workspace rules above.
github.rulesNoProjects: Create a team to set its automations.
github.syncRepoHelp: New issues of this repo (owner/name) land in this team, and closing, reopening, renaming and comments follow along. Older issues come in with the importer.
github.magicWords: In a PR title or body, "fixes WEB-12" (also closes, resolves, completes, implements) links and moves the issue; "ref WEB-12" or "part of WEB-12" only links it; "skip WEB-12" ignores it.

notifySettings.help: Your inbox gets everything. Choose what also reaches your email. This only affects you.
notifySettings.immediateHelp: An email a minute after something new lands, if you have not read it yet.
notifySettings.digestHelp: One email around 8:00 with what is still unread.
notifySettings.offHelp: No emails. The inbox keeps working as usual.

autoCycles.title: Automatic cycles
autoCycles.help: There is always a current cycle and the next one. When a cycle ends, its unfinished issues move to the current one.
autoCycles.prefixHelp: Cycles are numbered after this name.
autoCycles.adminOnly: Only workspace owners and admins can change this.

importer.title: Import issues
importer.lead: Bring issues from Linear, Jira, GitHub or a CSV. You see a preview before anything is created.
importer.linearHelp: In Linear: Settings › Security & access › Personal API keys. Read access is enough.
importer.githubHelp: A fine-grained token with read access to Issues on that repository.
importer.tokenNote: Used only for this import. It is kept encrypted while the import reads your data and deleted right after.
importer.linearNote: Linear teams become teams and Linear projects become milestones.
importer.csvTooLarge: The CSV is over 4 MB. Split it and import each part.
importer.csvEmpty: The file has no header row.

csvHelp.linear_csv: In Linear: Settings › Workspace › Import and export › Export CSV.
csvHelp.jira_csv: In Jira: Filters › Export › Export CSV (all fields).
csvHelp.csv: First row with column names. Up to 4 MB.

importer.csvRows: {count, plural, one {# row} other {# rows}}, {columns, plural, one {# column} other {# columns}}
importer.mappingHelp: Pick the column that fills each field. Title is required.
importer.already: {count, plural, one {# issue was imported before and will be skipped.} other {# issues were imported before and will be skipped.}}
importer.truncated: The source has more issues than one import accepts. The rest were left out.
importer.unmatchedNote: {count, plural, one {# assignee is not a member of this workspace. Their issues are imported without an assignee.} other {# assignees are not members of this workspace. Their issues are imported without an assignee.}}
importer.doneSummary: {issues, plural, one {# issue} other {# issues}} and {comments, plural, one {# comment} other {# comments}} imported, {skipped, number} skipped.
importer.doneUnassigned: {count, plural, one {# issue had an assignee who is not a member and was left unassigned.} other {# issues had an assignee who is not a member and were left unassigned.}}
importer.exportLead: Download issues as a CSV with the same columns the import reads.
importer.jiraQueryHelp: A project key like ENG imports that project. You can also paste a JQL query, for example project = ENG AND created >= 2024-01-01.
importer.jiraHelp: Create it at id.atlassian.com › Security › API tokens. It reads with the permissions of that account.
importer.asanaProjectHelp: Paste the project URL from the browser or its numeric id.
importer.asanaHelp: In Asana: profile photo › Settings › Apps › Developer apps › Create new token.
importer.asanaNote: Sections become statuses and tags become labels. Subtasks that live only inside a task are not imported.
importer.shortcutQueryHelp: A Shortcut search such as team:mobile or epic:"Onboarding". Empty imports every story that is not archived.
importer.shortcutHelp: In Shortcut: Settings › Your account › API tokens.
importer.shortcutNote: Each workflow becomes a team and epics become milestones. Shortcut caps how many stories one search returns: in a large workspace, import by team or epic.

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.adminOnly: Only workspace admins can change integrations.
integrations.disconnectConfirm: Disconnect {name}? Linked items stay on the issues.
integrations.keepSecret: Saved. Leave empty to keep it.
integrations.missingToken: Paste the API token to connect.

slack.help: Create issues from Slack messages and /track, get team updates in channels, sync comment threads and preview issue links.
slack.notConfigured: Slack is not set up on this server yet (SLACK_CLIENT_ID, SLACK_CLIENT_SECRET and SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET).
slack.howTo: In Slack: /track <title> creates an issue in the default team; on any message, More actions › Create Track issue opens a form and keeps the thread in sync with the issue comments.
slack.unfurl: Show a preview of issue links
slack.noChannels: No channels yet. Pick a team, a channel and what to post.
slack.disconnectConfirm: Disconnect Slack? Channel notifications stop and threads stop syncing.

sentry.help: New Sentry issues create a Track issue with the error link, and completing it resolves the issue in Sentry.
sentry.autoResolve: Resolve the Sentry issue when the Track issue is completed
sentry.steps: In Sentry: Settings › Developer Settings › New Internal Integration. Give it Issue & Event read and write, turn on the issue webhook, paste the webhook URL that appears here after connecting, and copy its client secret and token. To create issues only from alerts, add the integration as an action of an alert rule.
sentry.missingSecret: Paste the client secret to connect.

zendesk.help: Link Zendesk tickets to issues (paste the ticket URL in the issue, or send links when creating by API). When the issue is completed or cancelled, the ticket gets an internal note with the link.
zendesk.steps: In Zendesk: Admin Center › Apps and integrations › Zendesk API › Add API token. To create issues from Zendesk, add a trigger with a webhook to POST /api/v1/track/issues and the ticket URL in links.

intercom.help: Link Intercom conversations to issues. When the issue is completed or cancelled, the conversation gets an internal note with the link. Conversations of zerosoft Chat already create issues on their own.
intercom.adminId: Admin id that signs the notes
intercom.steps: In Intercom: Settings › Integrations › Developer Hub › your app › Authentication, copy the access token. The admin id is in the URL of your teammate profile.

figma.help: Paste a Figma file or design link in an issue description or comment and the issue shows it with a live preview. Private files open for whoever is signed in to Figma.

zapier.title: Zapier, Make and others
zapier.help: Outgoing webhooks send issue, comment and team events signed, with retries. The API creates and updates issues. Both work from Zapier, Make or n8n with a Webhooks step.

apiSettings.apiHelp: Issues, comments, teams, cycles, statuses, labels and people. Use an API key with the track:read or track:write scope; it acts as the person who created it, so it sees what that person sees.
apiSettings.webhooksHelp: issue.created, issue.updated, issue.status_changed, issue.deleted, comment.created and project.*, signed with Zerosoft-Signature, retried with backoff and with a log of each delivery.
apiSettings.webhooksLink: Set up webhooks in Workspace settings
apiSettings.mcpHelp: Connect Claude, Cursor or any MCP client over Streamable HTTP with an API key as Bearer token. Read-only keys or the readonly URL expose only the read tools.
apiSettings.mcpTools: Tools: search_issues, get_issue, create_issue, update_issue, add_comment, list_projects, get_project, list_cycles, list_labels, list_users.

access.title: Access
access.help: Private teams are visible only to their members. Guests see only the teams you give them.
access.adminOnly: Only workspace admins can change access.
access.personal: This is a personal workspace: nobody else sees your teams. Create a shared workspace in Settings to share teams and invite guests.
access.projectsHelp: Making a team private keeps you as a member and unsubscribes people who are not members. Admins see every team here and can join a private one.
access.guestsHelp: A guest is someone in your workspace who only sees the teams you check, for example a contractor or a client. You can mark the email before they accept the invitation.
access.guestEmailHelp: They also need a team invitation.
access.footnote: Integrations and API keys act as their owner and follow the same access.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.help: Who changed what in Track and from where: the app, the API, MCP, GitHub, Slack or Sentry.
audit.adminOnly: Only workspace admins can see the audit log.
audit.loadError: Could not load the audit log.
audit.emptyBody: Changes to issues, teams, access and integrations show up here.
